original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 4.7 Surface Plas: SPRi assay was performed to investigate the interactions between Ranacin and trypsin, thrombin, plasmin as well as plasma using a PlexArray HT A100 system (Plexera LLC, Bothell, Washington) as described in our previous study.32 Data were analyzed with the PLEXEA data analysis software.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Trypsin inhibitory and anticoagulant effects of Ranacin in vitro and in vivo assays. (A) Progress curves for trypsin proteolysis of the chromogenic substrate in the presence of the indicated concentrations of Ranacin. (B) Casein-agarose plate assay. (C, D) Representative SPRi sensorgrams of trypsin and plasma binding to Ranacin immobilized on a gold chip. (E) PRT assay. (F) APTT assay. The data are expressed as mean ± SD (n = 3). ***p < 0.001 compared with the control group treated with PBS. (G) Effect of Ranacin on platelet aggregation induced by thrombin. (H, I) Typical images and statistical results of mean intensity of isolated pancreatic sections in mice injected by fluorescent microspheres. The animals were injected with Ranacin 5 mg/kg or vehicle (0.9% saline), and immediately induced AP by two intraperitoneal injections of l-Arg (2.5 g/kg, 1 h interval) before they were injected intravenously with 2.5 μm fluorescent microspheres and their pancreas tissues were taken out to acquire the fluorescence images at 24 h post injection. The color from red to blue indicates the change of fluorescence intensity. The data are expressed as mean ± SD (n = 3). #p < 0.05 indicates the significant difference between the AP model group and the control group; *p < 0.05 compared with AP model group. (J, K) Typical pictures of carotid artery blood flow and statistical results of complete vessel occlusion time of FeCl3-treated mice. Mice were i.p. administrated with 0.9% saline (vehicle), heparin (200 U/kg), or Ranacin (5 mg/kg) 1 h before mice were treated by FeCl3 to induce thrombus formation and their blood flow was monitored for 12 min with laser speckle perfusion imaging. Red: blood flow; blue and black area: background. The data are expressed as mean ± SD (n = 4). *p < 0.05 and **p < 0.01 compared with the control group.
original_paragraph.Figure 3C: The x-axis is labeled 'Time (s)' and ranges from 0 to 600. The y-axis is labeled 'Response (RU)' and ranges from -100 to 300. Three curves are shown: black (10 μM), blue (20 μM), and red (40 μM). All curves show a rapid increase in response, reaching a plateau, followed by a decrease. The plateau response increases with concentration (black < blue < red).
original_paragraph.Figure 3D: The x-axis is labeled 'Time (s)' and ranges from 0 to 600. The y-axis is labeled 'Response (RU)' and ranges from -2000 to 6000. Four curves are shown: black (5%), blue (10%), green (20%), and red (40%). All curves show a rapid increase in response, reaching a plateau, followed by a decrease. The plateau response increases with concentration (black < blue < green < red).
